messages:
sara: heads up — after v2.3 driver rollout i see a tail-latency spike for short sequences when kv-cache is enabled (p95 up ~3x). attaching quick profiler snip and a stack of observations. anyone seen this pattern before?

anil: can you paste the profiler output and the kernel-selector decisions? curious if it's picking the heavier kernel for tiny seqs.

sara: sure. profiler (timeline):
```
seq=8 requests: kernel=matmul_fused_v2 @ 90%
seq=8 requests: when cache hit -> kernel switched to arch_opt_kernel_v3 (higher setup overhead)
seq=64 requests: kernel=arch_prefetch_v1 (expected)
```
also metrics: p50 ~18ms p95 ~120ms p99 ~260ms (baseline pre-rollout p95 ~40ms)

anil: interesting — looks like the selector now prefers v3 on cache hits for seq<=16. that would explain setup overhead. did we change kernel scoring weights in v2.3?

sara: not in the runtime core. but driver handshake added a new "capabilities" bit for persistent-kv that maps to an arch tag. might have caused a match to v3 in selector rules.

tom: looks like a classic feature-flag fallout. selector flow: capability tag -> candidate list -> cost model. if capability tag biases toward v3, even for short seq it may pick it. can we repro locally with the same capability header?

sara: repro script: `curl -H "X-RW-CAPS: kv_persist=1,arch=ampere_v3"` hitting /generate with seq=8 and prefilled kv-hit header. returns kernel_hint=v3 in logs. i can share trace.

jess: quick workaround: add a small rule in selector to prefer low-latency path for seq<=16 regardless of capability tag. we did that in an old patch. would be safe as a short-term fix.

anil: agree. longer-term we need to decouple kernel keying from driver capability bits: keying should be model+seqbin+quant_profile, not driver flags. otherwise persistence mismatches cause invisible perf switches.

sara: on keying: current cache key format is `ns|model:v|driver_caps_hash|seqbin|quant`. driver_caps_hash is the culprit. i propose we version the key: bump `key_schema=2` and make persistence migration explicit, and salt keys with a schema field.

rachel: +1 for explicit schema versioning. we should also add an invalidation handshake: when runtime upgrades with a different kernel set it emits `cache_schema_hint` so driver can decide to flush or continue with fallback. we hit trouble when drivers auto-upgrade and old cached entries route to incompatible kernels.

sara: for immediate steps: 1) revert selector weight change or add seq<=16 short-path override (canary to 10%); 2) release key_schema=2 that removes driver_caps_hash; 3) add migration job to expire old keys over 24h; 4) add runtime->driver cache_schema_hint in next patch.

tom: agree. i'll send a small patch to the selector with a hard-pref for seq<=16 and add a config flag `selector.strict_short_path=false` to toggle. canary it on dedicated first.

jess: i'll own the key_schema bump + migration job. plan: introduce `schema=2` which formats key as `ns|model:v|seqbin|quant|schema=2|salt`. migration: set TTL on old namespace keys to 6h, start writing new keys immediately. this avoids a big invalidation.

deploy-bot: deploy started by tom — selector-shortpath-fix -> canary group: dedicated-us-west-1 (5 pods).

anil: after canary we should run perf-profile smoke: 1k samples seq=8 with kv-hit and kv-miss, compare kernels, confirm p95 drops back. sara can you run that and paste numbers here?

sara: will run and post results in ~30m. initial local repro shows p95 down to ~38ms with the short-path override. will validate on canary infra.

rachel: also add a small dashboard alert rule: if kernel-choice changes distribution by >20% within 5m for a model, page eng-runtime. would catch this earlier next time.

sara: noted. thanks all — i'll follow up with the canary numbers and open a ticket for schema migration doc.
